exercise.name: Single Leg Calf Raise Off Step
aliases: Single-leg heel raise off a step

reference.title: Single Leg Calf Raise Off Step
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time: gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement comes from the name and standard coaching practice)

exercise.mechanics: Isolation (ankle plantarflexion on one leg through a full range)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the heel lowers below the step, breathe out as you rise onto the ball of the foot.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s down, short stretch, 1.3 s up, short pause

prescription.tempo: About 1-2 s down into the stretch, brief pause, 1 s up, 1 s squeeze
prescription.progression: Slower lowering, a longer stretch pause, then a dumbbell in the same-side hand.

cues.text: Stand on one foot with the ball of the foot on the edge of a step, heel off, hands lightly on a wall.
Breathe in and let the heel sink below the step for a calf stretch.
Pause briefly at the bottom without bouncing.
Breathe out and rise onto the ball of the foot as high as you can.
Pause at the top, then return to level under control.

mistakes.fix: Pause at the bottom and rise smoothly.
Rise as high as possible every rep.

mistakes.mistake: Foot rolling outward onto the little toe
mistakes.fix: Keep the pressure under the big toe and second toe.
Fingertips only steady you; the calf lifts the body.

kinematics.norm: Full range: below level into dorsiflexion at the bottom, full plantarflexion at the top; only full-height rises count in the heel-rise test (Hébert-Losier 2017)
As far as the range allows each rep (clinical opinion)
Straight but not locked; knee angle did not change triceps surae fatigue at 0 vs 45 degrees (Hébert-Losier 2012)
Light support with both hands on a wall for balance (clinical opinion)
About 1-2 s down, a short pause, about 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #11782, Single Leg Calf Raise Off Step, video (movement reference)

Hébert-Losier, Wessman, Alricsson & Svantesson 2017, updated reliability and normative values for the standing heel-rise test in healthy adults (Physiotherapy; doi 10.1016/j.physio.2017.03.002; PubMed 28886865)
Hébert-Losier, Schneiders, García, Sullivan & Simoneau 2012, influence of knee flexion angle and age on triceps surae muscle fatigue during heel raises (J Strength Cond Res 26(11))
Kinoshita, Maeo et al. 2023, triceps surae muscle hypertrophy is greater after standing versus seated calf-raise training (Front Physiol 14:1272106)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Achilles tendon pain: limit the drop below level and progress slowly.
Use a stable step with a non-slip edge.
modify: Balance: hold the wall more firmly.
Tender Achilles: stop at level (no drop below the step).
regressions: Two-leg calf raise off a step.

muscleNotes.calves_r: Gastrocnemius and soleus lift the body through a long range; standing calf-raise training grew the gastrocnemius more than seated work (Kinoshita 2023).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level on one leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Hold the free knee bent (clinical opinion).

phases.label: Rise onto the ball of the foot

guides.label: Heel drops, then rises about the ball of the foot
